# System Tray Integration with a Local Web Server

Dimension: Whether a system tray icon adds value vs a terminal command for a
localhost CLI-wrapper web app. Platform support on Linux GNOME and Windows 11.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## pystray: Primary Library

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Latest version | v0.19.5 [17] |
| Release date | Sep 17, 2023 [17] |
| Development status | "4 - Beta" [17] |
| Last release gap | ~2.5 years with no new release [17] |
| Maintenance | Low activity; multiple 2025 issues unanswered [17] |

### Platform Backends [18]

| Backend | Platform | Icon | Menu | Notifications |
|---------|----------|------|------|---------------|
| AppIndicator | Linux (GNOME with extension) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| GTK | Linux | May not show on GNOME | Yes | No |
| Xorg | Linux (X11) | Yes | No (default action only) | No |
| Win32 | Windows | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Darwin | macOS | Yes | Yes | No |

AppIndicator requires `gir1.2-ayatanaappindicator3-0.1` or equivalent typelib
packages at runtime [18].

### Threading Model [19]

- `Icon.run()` is blocking and must be called from the main thread [19]
- `run_detached()` available for integration with other event loops [19]
- `Icon.stop()` for shutdown [19]
- `Icon.HAS_NOTIFICATION` runtime check for notification support [19]

Known issue: `Icon.stop()` in threaded scenarios has reliability problems
(GitHub issue #94).

## GNOME System Tray Status

GNOME removed native system tray support in Shell 3.26.

| Extension | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| AppIndicator/KStatusNotifierItem | Most mature; preinstalled on Ubuntu | Reported broken on GNOME 48 (metadata comma error) |
| GNOME Status Icons (official) | Shipped with GNOME 47 | NOT enabled by default; NOT bundled unless distro includes it |
| Status Tray | Newer alternative | Uses modern GNOME APIs; self-contained |

**Key problem**: System tray on GNOME always requires an extension. This is
user-facing friction -- the app either requires the user to install an extension
or silently fails to show a tray icon.

A fork, pystray-freedesktop (v0.19.6a1), exists to improve Linux freedesktop.org
compatibility but its effectiveness at resolving the GNOME visibility issue is
unverified.

## Windows 11 Support

pystray's Win32 backend supports icons, menus, and notifications on Windows.
No UAC or notification area visibility issues were reported in any source, though
this was not specifically investigated.

## Tray vs Terminal Command

| Factor | Tray Icon | Terminal Command |
|--------|-----------|------------------|
| Persistent background presence | Yes | No (occupies terminal) |
| Single-instance enforcement | Via mutex locks | Via PID file |
| Browser launch | Click tray icon | webbrowser.open() on startup |
| Lifecycle management | Start/stop from menu | Ctrl+C / signal |
| Developer ergonomics | Lower (GUI interaction) | Higher (scriptable) |
| Dependencies | pystray + platform libs | None |
| GNOME compatibility | Requires extension | Works everywhere |
| Complexity | Higher (threading model) | Lower |

### Assessment

For a **developer-facing CLI tool**, a terminal command is the simpler, more robust
approach:

1. `python -m myapp serve` starts the server and opens the browser
2. Ctrl+C stops it cleanly via FastAPI lifespan shutdown [3]
3. No GNOME extension dependency
4. No pystray threading complexity
5. Scriptable and composable

A tray icon adds value primarily for **non-developer users** who want persistent
availability without a visible terminal window. Given the target audience (users
running `claude -p`), the terminal command is sufficient.

## Alternatives to pystray

| Alternative | Tray Support | Weight | Notes |
|-------------|--------------|--------|-------|
| Pyloid (PySide6) | Built-in | Heavy (~100MB PySide6) | More active than pystray; LGPL |
| QSystemTrayIcon (PyQt/PySide) | Full | Heavy (~100MB) | Requires Qt bindings |
| pywebview + pystray | Combination | Moderate | Webview wrapper + tray |
| Tauri (Rust shell) | Built-in | ~10MB | Requires Rust toolchain |
| desktop-notifier | Notifications only | Light | Complements pystray |

None of these alternatives are justified for a developer-facing tool where a
terminal command suffices. They introduce significant dependency weight for
marginal UX improvement.

## Recommendation

**Skip the tray icon.** Use a terminal command (`python -m myapp serve`) that:

1. Starts the FastAPI server on 127.0.0.1
2. Opens the default browser to the app URL
3. Handles Ctrl+C via lifespan shutdown [3]
4. Logs to the terminal for visibility

If tray support is later desired, pystray works but requires accepting:
- 2.5-year-old unmaintained library [17]
- GNOME extension dependency for Linux users
- Threading complexity with known stop() issues
- "4 - Beta" status [17]
